Palladium C atalysis Hot Paper
Palladium-Catalyzed [6+2] Double Allene Annulation for
Benzazocines Synthesis
Haibo Xu and Shengming Ma*
Abstract: An efficient double allene protocol for the
formation of benzazocines has been developed. The
reaction constitutes a highly regioselective palladium-
catalyzed formal [6+2] annulation of allenyl benzoxazi-
nanones with terminal allenes forming the challenging 8-
membered cycles. Decent yields and excellent regiose-
lectivity have been observed under mild conditions with
a remarkable Z-stereoselectivity for the exo-cyclic C = C
bonds. The synthetic potentials of benzazocine products
have been demonstrated.
E ight-membered cycles are attractive structural motifs in
natural products and small molecule drugs.
[1]
Taking benza-
zocine as an example, it serves as the core structure of a
variety of bio-active natural products, such as dehydro-
isolongistrobin,
[1a]
sulpinine C,
[1b]
shearinine C,
[1c]
and aspor-
yzin A
[1i]
(Scheme 1a). The limited flexibility increases the
binding affinity of eight-membered cycles, while their well-
defined conformations improve the physicochemical
properties.
[2]
It is well-known that unfavorable enthalpic and
entropic factors have been the major stumbling block for the
synthesis of the eight-membered rings, thus much attention
has been focused on this topic.
[3, 4]
On the other hand, allenes
bearing a leaving group at α-position could react with
transition metal catalysts to generate the methylene-π-allylic
metal intermediate,
[5]
which may readily undergo substitu-
tion reaction with stabilized nucleophiles or non-stabilized
nucleophiles to give either allenes
[6, 7]
and/or conjugated 1,3-
dienes,
[8]
respectively (Scheme 1b). With our longstanding
interest in developing new catalytic reactions of 2,3-allenyl
derivatives,
[6c–f, 7e–l, 8m]
we envisaged that an insertion reaction
of such methylene-π-allylic metal intermediates with an
unsaturated C � C bond would generate intermediates Int-A
and/or Int-B (Scheme 1c). Herein, we wish to demonstrate
the first example of such a concept: the unexpected Pd-
catalyzed formal [6+2] annulation of allenyl benzoxazina-
nones with allenes providing benzazocine derivatives highly
efficiently with an exclusively Z stereoselectivity for non-
terminal exo-cyclic C = C bond via Int-B (Scheme 1d).
[9, 10]
The most favored 6-membered products via Int-A has not
been formed.
Initially, we employed the allenyl benzoxazinanone 1 a
and 1-phenylpropadiene 2 a as the model substrates. Un-
fortunately, when bidentate phosphorous ligands L1-L4
were used, no product was detected (Table 1, entries 1–4).
Interestingly, the use of monophosphine ligand, PPh
3
,
produced the non-favorable eight-membered ring product
(Z)-3 aa in 30 % yield, and interestingly the formation of the
expected six-membered product 3 aa’ was not observed
(Table 1, entry 5). Further screening of mono-phosphine
ligands showed that tri(fur-2-yl)phosphine L5 delivered a

(Table 1, entries 10–14). Finally, the yield of (Z)-3 aa was
further improved to 86 % when the reaction was carried out
on a 0.5 mmol scale (Table 1, entry 15).
Subsequently, the effect of the N-protecting group was
investigated: When Ac (1 b), Boc (1 c), Me (1 d) and Ts (1 e)
protected allenyl benzoxazinanones were used, no desired
product was observed with recovery of the corresponding
allenyl benzoxazinanones (Scheme 2), indicating the impor-
tance of the Ns group. The electron-withdrawing character
of Ns group may facilitate the oxidative addition of
palladium with the C � O bond and stabilize the negative
charge on nitrogen after the subsequent decarboxylation.
With the optimal reaction conditions in hand, diversified
terminal allenes
[11]
were investigated to examine the scope of
this reaction for benzazocine derivatives synthesis
(Scheme 3). Terminal aryl allenes bearing electron-donating
groups, such as methoxy (2 b) and methyl (2 c), electron-
withdrawing as well as synthetically versatile groups, such as
halogen (2 d–2 g), acetyl (2 h), ester (2 i) and cyano (2 j), on
the aryl ring all proved to work for this reaction, providing
the desired benzazocine derivatives (Z)-3 ab-(Z)-3 aj in 40–
80 % yields. The phenyl ring could also be replaced with a β-
(2 k) or α-naphthyl (2 l) group, affording the products (Z)-
3 ak and (Z)-3 al in 50 % and 58 % yields, respectively. For
those results with yields less than 50 %, it may be due to the
lower reactivities of the allenes 2 causing unmatched
reactivity leading to partial decomposition of allenyl benzox-
azinones 1 during the reactions, causing the lower yields of
reactions.
Furthermore, non-aryl terminal allenes also participated
in the reaction smoothly: Functionalized allenes such as 2,3-
allenoate (2 m) and allene with a functionalized alkyl group
(2 n) also worked well to deliver the corresponding products
(Z)-3 am and (Z)-3 an with 64 % and 68 % yields. Such a
reaction has also been applied to the late-stage modification
of eucalyptene A (2 o),
[12]
affording the corresponding
benzazocine derivative (Z)-3 ao in 40 % yield.
Considering the importance of fluorine atom in organic
skeleton,
[13]
we turned to explore the scope of different
fluorine-substituted allenyl benzoxazinanones 1 f–1 h, yield-
ing the desired benzazocines (Z)-3 fa-(Z)-3 ha, and (Z)-3 fc
in 41–67 % yields. The practicality of this method has been
demonstrated by performing the reaction of allenyl benzox-
azinanone 1 a and 1-phenylpropadiene 2 a on 4 mmol scale,
providing benzazocine (Z)-3 aa in 78 % yield (1.3872 g). The
structures of (Z)-3 aa and (Z)-3 am were confirmed by X-ray
single crystal analysis.
[14]
The synthetic potential of this methodology has been
demonstrated as shown in Scheme 4: the intermolecular
Diels–Alder reaction of (Z)-3 ag with PTAD (4-phenyl-
1,2,4-triazoline-3,5-dione) at room temperature provided the
tetracyclic benzazocine derivative 4 in 59 % yield;
[15]
interest-
ingly, by conducting the reaction at 120 ° C, (Z)-3 ag could
undergo a twofold Diels–Alder reaction with 3.0 equiv. of
PTAD to afford hexacyclic product 5 with an excellent
diastereoselectvity in 51 % yield. The structure of 5 was
confirmed by X-ray single crystal analysis.
[14]
To gain insight into the mechanism, some control experi-
ments have been carried out: When the reaction was
conducted in the absence of terminal allene under the
optimal conditions, the formation of the imagined six-
membered product 7 derived from the reductive elimination
of intermediate III (Scheme 6) was not observed (Scheme 5,
eq 1), only recovery of 1 a was detected. Compared with the
reaction described in entry 8 of Table 1, within the same

after the addition of allene 2 a. It showed that allene 2 a did
play an important role in promoting the decarboxylative
oxidative addition of 1 a. Replacing the terminal allene with
styrene or diphenylacetylene also led to recovery of 1 a only:
neither eight-membered product 8/10 nor six-membered 9/
11 was formed (Scheme 5, eqs 2 and 3). These results
revealed the unique reactivity of terminal allene for this
transformation.
A plausible mechanism is then proposed as shown in
Scheme 6. Pd

active species. Initially, it catalyzes the decarboxylation of
1 a to generate the methylene-π-allylpalladium zwitterion
II,
[5]
which may isomerize to form more stable benzocyclic
intermediate III. The highly regio- and stereoselective

insertion of the terminal C = C bond in terminal allene 2
generating intermediate IV over V may be rationalized by
the steric difference of the two C = C bond in allene and the
steric hindrance between R and the olefinic H in intermedi-
ate V. Subsequent reductive elimination of intermediate IV
in the presence of allene 2 would furnish the final product
benzazocine (Z)-3 and regenerates Pd/L(allene 2) species I
to complete this catalytic cycle. According to the data shown
in Scheme 5, the pre-coordination of allene to the Pd atom
is critical for this transformation. The favorable formation of
the 8-membered product 3 over the 6-membered 3’ is caused
by the exclusive formation of Intermediate III.
In conclusion, we have developed a completely new
reactivity of methylene-π-allyl palladium species: the Pd-
catalyzed [6+2] annulation of allenyl benzoxazinanones with
the terminal C = C bond in allenes provides a new concept
for the unexpected 8-membered ring formation affording
functionalized benzazocine derivatives. The synthetic poten-
tials of the products have been demonstrated. Control
experiments suggested that neither alkene nor alkyne may
replace allene to react with allenyl benzoxazinanone to
deliver the related products. This new synthesis strategy will
expedite the synthesis of eight-membered heterocycles for
drug discovery and promote studies on new types of
reactions of methylene-π-allyl palladium species. Currently
we are actively working on the factors controlling the
regioselectivity, the effect of ligand L6, and new reaction
patterns.
